newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia ETOL says '96 net eased 1.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia ETOL says '96 net eased 1.8 pct.

text.p: Slovenian aroma producer Etol said on Monday 1996 net profit eased to 177.6 million tolars ($1.1 million) from 180.9 million in the previous year.
"Profits were down because of the bankruptcy of bank Komercialna Banka Triglav (KBT), in which we had an eight percent stake," Brigita Cokl, the head of Etol's finance department, told Reuters.
KBT declared bankrupcty in July 1996 after running into liquidity problems.
Etol's board suggested a 1996 dividend of 603.75 tolars per share, from a 1995 dividend of 543.8 tolars. The shares went ex-dividend on Monday.
Etol's sales rose eight percent to 2.9 billion tolars. The group said 59.3 percent of sales were exported, mainly to the states of the former Yugoslavia and other eastern European countries.
Cokl said the company expected earnings to grow by over 10 percent this year as sales were expected to expand in all market segments. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
